questions.question: A and B can complete a piece of work in 15 days and 20 days respectively. If they work together for 3 days and then A leaves, in how many days will B alone complete the remaining work?

options.explanation: Incorrect. The remaining work is 39 units, and B's efficiency is 3 units/day, so time = 39/3 = 13 days.
Incorrect. The remaining work is 39 units, and B's efficiency is 3 units/day, so time = 39/3 = 13 days.
Correct. The remaining work is 39 units, and B's efficiency is 3 units/day, so time = 39/3 = 13 days.
Incorrect. The remaining work is 39 units, and B's efficiency is 3 units/day, so time = 39/3 = 13 days.

questions.explanation: Total work = LCM of (15, 20) = 60 units. A's efficiency = 60/15 = 4 units/day. B's efficiency = 60/20 = 3 units/day. Combined efficiency of A and B = 4 + 3 = 7 units/day. Work done by A and B in 3 days = 7 units/day * 3 days = 21 units. Remaining work = 60 - 21 = 39 units. Time taken by B to complete the remaining work = 39 units / 3 units/day = 13 days.
questions.hint: Calculate the work done by A and B together in 3 days and then find the remaining work for B.
questions.subject: bank-quant

questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours, and Pipe B can fill it in 15 hours. Pipe C can empty the same tank in 20 hours. If all three pipes are opened together, how long will it take to fill the tank?

options.explanation: Incorrect. The net filling rate is 6 units/hour, so time = 60/6 = 10 hours.
Incorrect. The net filling rate is 6 units/hour, so time = 60/6 = 10 hours.
Correct. The net filling rate is 6 units/hour, so time = 60/6 = 10 hours.
Incorrect. The net filling rate is 6 units/hour, so time = 60/6 = 10 hours.

questions.explanation: Let the total capacity of the tank be the LCM of 12, 15, and 20, which is 60 units. Rate of Pipe A (filling) = 60 units / 12 hours = +5 units/hour. Rate of Pipe B (filling) = 60 units / 15 hours = +4 units/hour. Rate of Pipe C (emptying) = 60 units / 20 hours = -3 units/hour. Net filling rate when all three pipes are open = (+5) + (+4) + (-3) = 6 units/hour. Time taken to fill the tank = Total capacity / Net filling rate = 60 units / 6 units/hour = 10 hours.
questions.hint: Calculate the net rate of filling by adding the rates of all pipes, considering Pipe C empties the tank.
questions.subject: bank-quant

questions.question: P, Q, and R can complete a work in 10, 12, and 15 days respectively. They start the work together, but P leaves after 2 days. Q leaves 3 days before the completion of the work. In how many days is the work completed?

options.explanation: Incorrect. The total days calculated are 7.
Correct. The total days calculated are 7.
Incorrect. The total days calculated are 7.
Incorrect. The total days calculated are 7.

questions.explanation: Total work = LCM of (10, 12, 15) = 60 units. P's efficiency = 60/10 = 6 units/day. Q's efficiency = 60/12 = 5 units/day. R's efficiency = 60/15 = 4 units/day. Work done by P, Q, and R together in the first 2 days = (6 + 5 + 4) * 2 = 30 units. Remaining work = 60 - 30 = 30 units. After 2 days, P leaves. Q and R continue the work. Let 'x' be the number of days for which Q and R work together. Q leaves 3 days before completion, so R works alone for the last 3 days. Work done by R in the last 3 days = 4 * 3 = 12 units. Remaining work after R's last 3 days = 30 - 12 = 18 units. Combined efficiency of Q and R = 5 + 4 = 9 units/day. Days Q and R worked together = 18 / 9 = 2 days. Total days = 2 (all three) + 2 (Q and R) + 3 (R alone) = 7 days.
questions.hint: Calculate the work done in the first 2 days, then determine the remaining work and the time taken by Q and R together before Q leaves.
questions.subject: bank-quant

questions.question: A group of 12 men and 16 boys can do a piece of work in 5 days. 13 men and 24 boys can do the same work in 4 days. How many days will it take for 1 man and 1 boy to complete the work together?

options.explanation: Incorrect. The combined work rate is 3/200 per day, so time = 200/3 days.
Correct. The combined work rate is 3/200 per day, so time = 200/3 days.
Incorrect. The combined work rate is 3/200 per day, so time = 200/3 days.
Incorrect. The combined work rate is 3/200 per day, so time = 200/3 days.

questions.explanation: Let the work done by 1 man in 1 day be 'm' and by 1 boy in 1 day be 'b'. From the first condition: 12m + 16b = 1/5. From the second condition: 13m + 24b = 1/4. Solve the two equations: Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by 2: 36m + 48b = 3/5 and 26m + 48b = 1/2. Subtract the second from the first: 10m = 3/5 - 1/2 = 1/10. So, m = 1/100. Substitute m in the first equation: 12*(1/100) + 16b = 1/5 => 12/100 + 16b = 20/100 => 16b = 8/100 => b = 1/200. Combined work of 1 man and 1 boy in 1 day = m + b = 1/100 + 1/200 = 3/200. Time taken to complete the work = 1 / (3/200) = 200/3 days ≈ 66.67 days.
questions.hint: Set up equations based on the given conditions and solve for the work rates of a man and a boy.
